body.div:
August 26, 15 My dear Mr. Fletcher:
The cheque I sent you was for your share of the vast profits made by the Imagist Anthology. It was for $28.63, if I remember right. I sent it to Bay View, and probably your family have forwarded it to you by this time. But if the thing is really lost, let me know, and I will stop payment on the cheque and send you another.
Your clippings were very interesting. I think you did quite well to write to “The Dial,” and I liked your letter. Richard writes me that we have had two reviews in Russian papers, one already published, and one coming, and he understands that Prince Kuropatkin likes us. “The Times” was a slam, of course; what can you expect?
I envy you your trip down the Mississippi. I have done about fifty pages of translations, and I think that is only a little over half. Still, we are getting through, and I probably shall be found turning somersaults down Commonwealth Avenue from sheer exuberance of spirits when I get done. I am going down this afternoon to see about various papers and paper-hangers, and I shall not be able therefore to sign this letter so forgive me if it goes without signature.
It is a bully, late-summer day up here. You would like it: clear air, and the distant hills looking as if you could touch them;
wind, big white clouds, and the yellowest goldenrod I ever beheld. “Fresh washed and fair” but in an entirely different way from the Spring way.
This is only a little bit of a note, written just as I am starting. I do envy you your trip and the poems that will come out of it. Affectionately yours, Dictated but not signed by Miss Lowell.
